name: CMS Energy Corporation
moat_justification: Exclusive Michigan regulated franchise (Consumers Energy electric + gas monopolies) with captive essential-service demand and a $24.1B capex program through 2030 that compounds rate base — a durable, visible earnings machine, and management guides 6-8% long-term EPS growth. Capped at 6 because the regulator, not the company, sets returns: the MPSC granted 9.8% ROE and $139M of a $240M request in the Oct 2026 gas case, the Attorney General intervenes against increases, and the build is funded with $18,248M of net debt plus recurring equity issuance (share count +1.25%/yr) — durability is high, pricing power is nil.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

one_liner: Durable Michigan regulated monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative on every base (TTM -$3.66/share, normalized -$2.52/share, latest FY -$2.69/share) because capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — Tier F on this screen; guided 6-8% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated Michigan franchise — Consumers Energy holds monopoly electric and gas service territories with captive, essential-service demand
Rate-base compounding: the $24.1B planned capital program through 2030 (10-K) enters rate base and earns a regulator-allowed return
Michigan's 2023 clean-energy law locks in a multi-decade investment runway (renewables, storage, grid, gas safety)
Regulatory recovery is recurring in practice: a $277M electric increase took effect May 2026 and a $139M gas increase was approved Oct 2026 (search results)
moat_against: No pricing power: the MPSC sets the allowed ROE (9.8% granted in the Oct 2026 gas case) and granted $139M of a $240M gas request — returns are capped and political, with the Michigan AG intervening in rate cases
Growth is externally funded: net debt $18,248M and a share count growing 1.25%/yr from recurring equity issuance dilute per-share compounding
Capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow, so the build depends on continuous capital-market access
Single-state concentration: Michigan weather (Q2 2026 earnings fell on mild weather), affordability politics, and storm costs all sit with the equity
